SL-000005.transcript:
Member (Mathieu Martin): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Mathieu Martin, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Martin): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Martin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mathieu Martin): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How old is he?
Member (Mathieu Martin): Fourteen.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Mathieu Martin): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Mathieu Martin): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Mathieu Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Mathieu Martin): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Mathieu Martin): Great, that helps.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Mathieu Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000005.narrative_summary: Mathieu Martin, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a coverage question case. Agent Chloe Gagnon checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

Member (Lucas O'Brien): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Lucas O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Lucas O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Lucas O'Brien): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Lucas O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Lucas O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Lucas O'Brien): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Lucas O'Brien): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Lucas O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000106.transcript:
Member (Liam Fortin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Liam Fortin, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Fortin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Liam Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Fortin): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Liam Fortin): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Liam Fortin): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Liam Fortin): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Liam Fortin): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Liam Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Liam Fortin): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Liam Fortin): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Liam Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Chantal Patel): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Chantal Patel): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Chantal Patel): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Chantal Patel): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Chantal Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Chantal Patel): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Chantal Patel): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Chantal Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Wilson): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Emma Wilson, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Wilson): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Emma Wilson): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Emma Wilson): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Emma Wilson): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Emma Wilson): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has the dental office called us about this directly?

Member (Emma Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Emma Wilson): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Emma Wilson): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Emma Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Morrison): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Leila Morrison, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Morrison): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.

Member (Leila Morrison): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.

Member (Noah Singh): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which plan is the transfer from?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you send in the transfer request?

Member (Noah Singh): Who follows up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Noah Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Liam Patel): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Liam Patel, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Patel): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Liam Patel): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Liam Patel): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Liam Patel): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Liam Patel): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Liam Patel): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you in any pain right now?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Liam Patel): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Liam Patel): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Liam Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Liam Martin): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.

Member (Liam Martin): I don't know who my case manager is.

Member (Liam Martin): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.

Member (Liam Martin): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?

Member (Emma Chen): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Emma Chen, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Emma Chen): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Emma Chen): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Emma Chen): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Emma Chen): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Emma Chen): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Emma Chen): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Emma Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Ahmed): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Hannah Ahmed, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.

Member (Hannah Ahmed): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Hannah Ahmed): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.

Member (Hannah Ahmed): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Member (Hannah Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Owen Morrison): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Fortin): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Emma Fortin, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Emma Fortin): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.

Member (Tyler Patel): I'm following up again — my Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Liam Wilson): I'm following up again — my Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Liam Wilson, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Wilson): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Liam Wilson): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Liam Wilson): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Liam Wilson): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Liam Wilson): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Liam Wilson): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Liam Wilson): They said they called and got the same answer as me.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Liam Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Liam Wilson): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Liam Wilson): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Liam Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma O'Brien): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Fatima Lavoie, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): When did you go off work?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've asked for a call-back once the trace is complete, and you'll also see it in the app.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: a payment trace is open, it can take up to ten business days, and you'll get a call when it's done.
Member (Noah Morrison): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

SL-002868.transcript:
Member (Noah Campbell): I'm following up again — my dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Noah Campbell, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Campbell): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Noah Campbell): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah Campbell): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Noah Campbell): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Noah Campbell): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Noah Campbell): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Member (Noah Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Noah Campbell): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Noah Campbell): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Noah Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-002958.transcript:
Member (Arjun Fortin): I'm following up again — I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Arjun Fortin, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Fortin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Arjun Fortin): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Arjun Fortin): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Arjun Fortin): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Arjun Fortin): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Arjun Fortin): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Arjun Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Arjun Fortin): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Arjun Fortin): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Arjun Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Martin): I'm following up again — my dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.

Member (Arjun Martin): I already explained this on my last contact.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Arjun Martin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
